newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Youth charged over Qantas bomb extortion threat.
newsitem.headline: Youth charged over Qantas bomb extortion threat.

text.p: A 17-year-old youth appeared in an Australian court on Sunday on a charge of trying to extort A$505,000 (US$379,000) from Qantas Airways Ltd with a threat to detonate a bomb on an aircraft flying from Sydney to Hong Kong on Friday.
A police prosecutor told an out-of-hours Children's Court hearing that police found information from the Internet on bomb-making at the youth's home when he was arrested.

"He has accessed the Internet, where he has gleaned information relating to terrorist-type activity and gained information relating to the construction and detonation of explosive devices," prosecution sergeant Dave Perry told the court.

Perry said the teenager, from Belmore in Sydney's west, allegedly demanded payment of A$505,000 in used bank notes from Qantas or he would detonate by remote control a bomb he said he had placed on Qantas Flight 27, which had left Sydney for Hong Kong on Friday afternoon.
Perry did not tell the court whether a bomb was actually on the aircraft, which carried 95 passengers plus crew, and a Qantas spokeswoman said she could not make any comment.
The youth phoned Qantas about one-and-a-half hours after the flight's departure and made the threat using the pseudonym "Mr Brown", Perry said.
The youth was not named because of his age. He did not enter a plea and was remanded in custody.
